core.title: List only declared product capabilities in a user/system flow
core.given: A non-excluded plan artifact contains a user/system flow whose product capability list names product capabilities (changed or not).
core.when: The plan is authored, edited or checked — a user/system flow's product capability list is written, a product capability declaration is renamed or removed, or existing plans are validated.
core.then: Every product capability the user/system flow's product capability list names is declared as a product capability declaration with a matching product capability URN.
prefer: Declare the missing product capability as a product capability declaration.
Or remove the product capability from the user/system flow.
When renaming or removing a product capability declaration, update every user/system flow that lists it in the same change.
avoid: Listing a product capability in a user/system flow that has no product capability declaration — a user/system flow ordering a product capability that does not exist cannot run.
Declaring an empty placeholder product capability solely to silence the check instead of planning the product capability or removing it from the user/system flow.
unless: Vendored and generated trees are never scanned (the stack-wide exclusion list, profile: roots.excluded).
core.why: A user/system flow ordering a product capability that does not exist cannot run. Product capability membership is the train-specific case of reference resolution.
evidence: The stack's plan-integrity check reports no unresolved user/system flow product capability across all non-excluded plans.
For each product capability named in each user/system flow's product capability list, a reviewer finds a matching product capability declaration.
The rule has a failing fixture (a user/system flow listing an undeclared product capability) that the check rejects.
verification: Check: every entry in a scanned user/system flow's product capability list must match a declared product capability URN; any unmatched entry is a finding.
Scan scope: applies to every scanned user/system flow, not only changed ones; pre-existing unresolved product capability references are findings regardless of what the current edit touched.
Never scan the stack-wide excluded vendored and generated trees (profile: roots.excluded); the exact classification of what is vendored or generated is owned by the stack's checker.

Enforced by the stack's plan-integrity check, held to the same per-rule checks as every convention: a statement, strict disposition, a failing fixture, relationship edges. The concrete detector, validator and finding ids of this rule are realization details.

values: plan integrity check: unresolved user/system flow product capability
user/system flow product capability list added or edited
product capability declaration renamed or removed

fires: Checking any non-excluded plan, including an unchanged one, whose user/system flow's product capability list already names a product capability with no matching product capability declaration.
A planner edits only a product capability's content in a plan where some user/system flow already lists an undeclared product capability — the pre-existing unresolved reference is still a finding.
A planner adds a product capability reference to a user/system flow's product capability list without a matching product capability declaration in the plan.
A planner renames or deletes a product capability declaration while a user/system flow still lists the old reference.
A user/system flow lists a product capability reference with a typo that matches no declared product capability.
doesNotFire: Every product capability named in every non-excluded user/system flow's product capability list has a matching product capability declaration.
Plan-like artifacts inside the stack's never-scanned vendored and generated trees (profile: roots.excluded).

Edits to a product capability's content that keep its product capability declaration, provided every user/system flow product capability reference in the scanned plans resolves to a declared product capability (pre-existing unresolved references still fire).

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack-wide list of vendored and generated trees that are never scanned — the only exception to this rule.

The concrete plan-artifact construct by which a user/system flow lists the product capabilities it orders (the capability-membership list).

neutralityNotes: 'User/system flow' and 'product capability' are treated as stack-neutral planning vocabulary (both are artifact kinds in the closed urn group); only their concrete syntax is profile-driven: the `capabilities:` list via the proposed idiom.plan_syntax#user_system_flow_capability_list and the `capability:<slug>` declaration via urn.capability. The exact excluded trees exist only as the roots.excluded profile value; the checker keeps ownership of classifying them. Validator/finding ids and the package-guard-vs-canonical-planner-node enforcement split stay Bun-only: which component owns the plan-integrity check is a realization choice, so the core requires the check without restricting its owner. The alias and audit metadata stay Bun-only. Severity '3' is kept as declared because severity and disposition belong to the rule, though the numeric scale itself is a convention of this package family.
